creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The seam pushes one pane's agent state and takes one pane's input. A
window showing a tree needs to be told the tree, and a person who wants
a split needs somewhere to ask for one.

Out: the whole region tree, absolute and idempotent, in the same
discipline the daemon's own events follow - split nodes with direction
and ratio, pane leaves carrying id, agent state and that pane's control
socket. Whole-view rather than incremental is what keeps the shell
dumb. proto/muster.proto already anticipates this in a comment on
PaneStateChanged.

In: split, close, focus and set-split-ratio. herdr answers all four
already (pane.split, pane.close, pane.focus, layout.set_split_ratio),
so what this adds is the core dispatching them - which is where "one
action path" stops being a principle and becomes the thing a CLI and an
agent-facing API will reuse verbatim.
title: 🔌 The seam grows a view, and a way to act on it
